summary: A waḍīn is a wide girth, made of woven thongs, hair, or skin. It's used for securing a camel's saddle (raḥl) or a litter (hawdaj), similar to how a biṭān is used for a pack-saddle (qatab).
lane: وَضِينٌ ذ A girth ( بِطَان ) wide, woven of thongs or hair, or only of skin; (M, K;) said to be adapted for the رَحْل and the هَوْدَج ; the بِطَان being peculiarly for the قَتَب : (M:) or it is for the هَوْدَج , like the بِطَان for the قَتَب and the تَصْدِير for the رَحْل and the حِزَام for the سَرْج ; and both [but to what this refers is doubtful] are like the نِسْع , except that they are of thongs woven one upon another, doubly or more. (S.)
